page: Amazon Web Services m9g.medium is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. It features a single dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) utilizing an AWS Neoverse-V3 processor operating at 3.3 GHz. The CPU architecture is configured with a 64 KB L1 data cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware cryptographic acceleration enabled. The instance provides 4.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM general-purpose ratio. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external network storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect the strong per-core efficiency of the Neoverse-V3 core balanced against the architectural limits of a single-core instance. Single-threaded evaluation demonstrates top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing (2239.0) as well as decompression and compression tests, including 36.08 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 17.04 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Conversely, overall multi-core throughput is constrained by the single-thread allocation, recording lower tiers in multi-core stress-ng (1988.18) and PassMark CPU metrics (1408.64). Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 43.27 GB/sec for uncached reads and 13.7 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.medium provides an entry-level compute environment with dedicated CPU resources, avoiding the performance variability associated with shared-core burstable instances. The hardware configuration makes it suitable for lightweight microservices, small API gateways, single-worker task queues, test environments, and ARM-native software compilation pipelines that require predictable single-thread performance without multi-core overhead.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.medium is a general-purpose cloud instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a dedicated 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor at 3.3 GHz. Configured with 1 vCPU, 4.0 GB of system RAM, and 1 Gbps baseline network throughput, it contains no local disk storage or hardware accelerators. The instance delivers strong single-threaded throughput, registering top-tier results in Geekbench single-core processing and gzip decompression. However, aggregate compute and memory throughput remain restricted by the single-core topology, yielding lower multi-threaded benchmark rankings. Delivering dedicated CPU allocation at a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, the instance offers predictable resource density for lightweight workloads. It is functionally well-suited for containerized microservices, low-traffic web serving, development environments, and single-threaded ARM continuous integration pipelines.
